definition: A specific string or token that, when generated, signals a language model to halt further text generation.
details: Stop sequences are commonly configured in API calls to control output length and formatting, ensuring generation halts at a natural or application-defined boundary rather than continuing indefinitely.
story: Think of a jazz musician who has heard so many solos that a new one simply falls out of their fingers. Think of it this way: A specific string or token that, when generated, signals a language model to halt further text generation. And here is the clever part: Stop sequences are commonly configured in API calls to control output length and formatting, ensuring generation halts at a natural or application-defined boundary rather than continuing indefinitely. Creation, here, is memory recombined at speed. And that is Stop Sequence — making something new out of everything it has ever seen.
